question: Does matching a horse's demonstrated lap/RPCI profile to the pre-race expected RPCI and course demand improve OOS ranking beyond the current M3-like baseline?

protocol.target_universe: JRA flat 3-win class or higher, field size >=12, races with matched lap data and pre-race course history
protocol.model: ridge alpha=0.1, median imputation, standardized features
protocol.horse_history: previous 5 starts only, strictly before target date
protocol.expected_rpci: past-only expanding mean by venue x surface x distance x going, fallback venue x surface x distance
protocol.expected_course_demand: past-only lap-demand profile for the same course, preferentially within the expected RPCI band; no current-race realized laps used

models.M0: current M3-like baseline using pre-race position/closing-history features and validated remaining-600m gap
models.MCAP: M0 + generic lap-capacity history (acceleration, sustain, peak speed, deceleration resistance, back-5F push)
models.FRPCI: M0 + generic lap capacity + pre-race course context + performance in prior starts from the same expected RPCI band
models.FULL: FRPCI + direct acceleration/sustain/peak-speed course-demand interaction terms

simple_descriptive_flag.definition: within previous 5 starts, at least one start in the expected RPCI band, with positive race-relative final-3F and average finish percentile <=0.5
simple_descriptive_flag.note: Flagged horses were also more popular on average, so these raw rates are descriptive only; the paired ranking-model comparison above is the main evidence.

interpretation: The stable additional signal is stronger for RPCI-regime matching than for raw acceleration/sustain interaction alone.
Spearman and pairwise ranking improve in 2024, 2025 and 2026; pooled confidence intervals are fully positive.
Top-3 overlap improves in all three years and is clearly positive in the 2026 holdout; pooled improvement is about +1.8 percentage points.
Winner top-1 is not stable: it improves in 2024, declines in 2025 and is unchanged in 2026 for FRPCI.
Therefore this should not yet alter calibrated win/top2/top3 probabilities or replace the M3 FinishScore core.

decision.recommended_use: show expected RPCI band and prior same-band performance; use as auxiliary/tie-break context only until a future untouched season confirms winner/top1 stability
